II. Some H are Q.

I. Some Q are N.

II. Some Q are H.

options.text: Both conclusions I and II follows

Conclusion:

I. Some Q are N - True (Because All N are Q, so some Q are also N).

II. Some Q are H - True (Because Some H are Q, it means Some Q are also H).

Hence, the correct answer is **"Option 2"**.

questions.question:
Which of the following statement is correct regarding large dams?

I. They have social problems because they displace large number of peasants and tribals without adequate compensation or rehabilitation.

II. They have Environmental problems because they contribute enormously to deforestation and the loss of biological diversity.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **__2) Both I and II.__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__****Understanding the statements in relation to large dams**

__
 
• **Social Problems**

 
 
• Large dams have significant social impacts, particularly on the lives of peasants and tribal communities.
 
• The construction of large dams often necessitates the displacement of large populations from their ancestral lands.
 
• Many affected individuals and communities face inadequate compensation and lack proper rehabilitation plans.* Hence statement I is correct.*
 
 
 
• **Environmental Problems**
 
 
• The construction and operation of large dams can have profound environmental consequences.
 
• They often lead to extensive deforestation, which in turn reduces biodiversity by destroying habitats.
 
• This loss of forests and biological diversity can disrupt local ecosystems and contribute to larger environmental issues.* Hence statement II is correct.*
 
 

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] Additional Information__**

 
• **Impacts on Local Communities**

 
 
• The construction of large dams can disrupt local economies that are dependent on traditional practices and occupations.
 
• The disruption can lead to long-term socio-economic challenges for the displaced populations.
 
 
 
• **Hydrological Changes**
 
 
• Large dams alter the natural flow of rivers, which can impact the water availability downstream.
 
• These hydrological changes can negatively affect agriculture, fisheries, and the natural sediment transport, leading to further environmental degradation.

__
 
• **ROM**

 
 
• Read-Only Memory is a ROM in a computer.
 
• Read-only memory is a storage medium that permanently stores data on computers and electronic devices.
 
• The data stored in these chips is nonvolatile i.e. it is not lost when power is removed.
 
• There are five basic ROM types:
 
 
• ROM: Read-Only Memory.
 
• PROM: Programmable read-only memory.
 
• EPROM: Erasable programmable read-only memory.
 
• EEPROM: Electrically erasable programmable read-only memory.
 
• Flash memory: Flash memory, a type of EEPROM that uses in-circuit wiring. 
 
 
 
• BIOS uses Flash memory.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• The smallest and fastest memory of a computer is registered memory located in the computer's central processing unit(CPU).
 
• It generally stores the most used instructions, data, etc. which are to be used by CPU.
 
• Control Unit is part of the CPU.
 
• It advises the input and output devices, and computer memory on how to respond to the instructions sent to the processor.
 
 
 
• **RAM**
 
 
• It stores data that the computer needs to use temporarily. So it is faster than the secondary storage devices. It is a volatile memory i.e. the data disappear from it when the power is off.
 
• It is known as the Read-Write Memory. i.e. the user can write information into RAM and read information from it.
 
• It is called random access since any memory location can be accessed randomly for reading and writing. The access time is the same for each memory location.
 
• It is usually called “temporary” memory, which means that when the system is shut down, the memory is lost.
 
 
 
• **Cache**
 
 
• A cache memory is used by the central processing unit of a computer to reduce the average cost time or energy to access data from the** main memory**. 
 
• Generally Cache memory is logically positioned between** CPU** and **main memory**.
